title: observability: token-level KV cost & latency dashboard, tracing instrumentation, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds a token-level KV cache cost and latency dashboard, improves tracing spans for KV cache hits/misses, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce noise for autoscaling and cost teams. Motivation: teams have been unable to correlate per-token KV cache behavior with token-level cost and tail latency in production; noisy alerts were causing paging during routine node rebalances. This PR includes: 1) New Grafana dashboard JSON (observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json) with token-level histograms, p95/p99 latency heatmaps, and per-model cost breakdown; 2) Additional Prometheus metrics (telemetry/metrics/kv_metrics_collector.go) exposing token_cache_hits_total, token_cache_misses_total, token_kv_cost_tokens_total and token_kv_latency_seconds_bucket labeled by model, shard, and route; 3) Tracing instrumentation (telemetry/tracing/kv_span_instrumentation.go) to surface KV hit/miss spans with attributes for cold_warm_hit, kv_backend, and cache_ttl; 4) Alert tuning YAML (observability/alerts/kv_cache_alerts.yaml) that debounces alerts, adds dynamic thresholds based on baseline traffic, and creates separate severity levels for cost and latency regressions; 5) Documentation update with rollout and runbook steps (docs/observability/token_kv_dashboard.md). Checklist: - [x] Metrics schema reviewed with infra and SRE - [x] Dashboard panels validated with staging traces - [x] Alerts tested by synthetic traffic and monkeypatching quotas - [x] Backwards-compatible metric names and labels - [x] Updated runbook and playbook entries Rollout notes: deploy metrics collector, wait 10m for baseline, then apply dashboards and alert rules. Monitor errors and increase debounce window if false positives observed.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial metrics collector and proto wireup; add dashboard JSON and panels; tracing spans and tests; alert rules and debounce logic; docs and changelog. Key commits: 1) add token kv metrics 2) dashboard panels + panel links 3) trace span attributes + unit tests 4) alert tuning + debouncing middleware 5) docs and runbook
review_comments: Ethan Chen: LGTM overall, left one question on cardinality for model label - can we ensure model label is hashed for high-cardinality routes?
Aisha Patel (author): Good catch - we switched model -> model_hash in the collector and documented the mapping in pkg/telemetry/metrics/README.md. Updated tests to assert label cardinality bound.

Maya Thompson: Alert debounce looks better but we still see noise on canary bursts. Suggest increasing the debounce to 5m for severity=warning and adding a rolling-avg-based suppression for traffic spikes.
Aisha Patel (author): Increased debounce to 5m for warning, added rollingAvg suppression window and unit tests that simulate spike scenarios. Verified in staging with synthetic traffic.
Ravi Kapoor: Integration tests failed initially due to missing Prometheus histogram buckets; tests now pass after adding explicit bucket boundaries. Approving after CI green.
Automation Bot: ci/lint originally failed on telemetry/tracing/kv_span_instrumentation.go; fixes applied in commit 4 to satisfy linters.
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and tracing for cost and latency analysis
New Grafana dashboard: Token KV Cost & Latency with per-model breakdowns
Alert tuning: debounce windows and dynamic thresholds to reduce noisy paging
Documentation and runbook added for rollout and incident response
notes_for_ops: Rollout order: 1) deploy telemetry collector and migration job for model->model_hash mapping 2) wait 10 minutes for baseline metrics to populate 3) apply dashboard JSON and alert rules 4) monitor alerts for 24h and increase debounce window if noise persists. If high-cardinality metrics appear, revert the model label change and contact telemetry@redwood.internal.
